examples.ko: 끝없이 펼쳐진 광야에 말을 탄 사람들이 보였어요.
examples.en: I saw people on horseback on the endless open plain.

examples.ko: 광야를 달리는 기차 창밖으로 지평선이 보였어요.
examples.en: Through the window of the train running across the wilderness, I could see the horizon.

examples.ko: 개척자들은 낯선 광야를 건너 새 땅을 찾아갔어요.
examples.en: The pioneers crossed an unfamiliar wilderness to find new land.
On the plain, nothing could be heard except the sound of the wind.

examples.ko: 성경에는 사람들이 광야에서 40년을 떠돌았다는 이야기가 나와요.
examples.en: The Bible tells a story of people wandering in the wilderness for forty years.

examples.ko: 혼자 광야 같은 도시에 던져진 기분이었어요.
examples.en: I felt as if I had been thrown alone into a city like a wilderness.

explain: 나무나 건물이 거의 없는 넓고 거친 들판이에요. '들판', '벌판'과 비슷하지만 '광야'는 더 크고 황량한 느낌이라 시, 소설, 역사 이야기에서 많이 나와요. 비유로 막막하고 외로운 상황을 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: Only the wind blows across the wide wilderness.
phrases.nuance_ko: '광야'의 크기를 말할 때 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing to describe its vastness.

phrases.en: He walked alone across the wilderness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기나 시에서 외로운 여행을 표현할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits stories and poems describing a lonely journey.

phrases.example: 눈 덮인 벌판이 끝없이 펼쳐져 있어요.
phrases.en: A snow-covered field stretches on endlessly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '광야'와 비슷하지만 덜 황량하고 더 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 광야 but less desolate and more everyday.

explain_en: It is a wide, rough stretch of land with few trees or buildings. It is similar to '들판' and '벌판', but '광야' feels bigger and more desolate, so it appears in poems, novels and historical stories. It can also describe a bleak, lonely situation figuratively.

p.n: 광야 feels vaster and more desolate; 들 is ordinary open countryside.

examples.en: Strange rocky cliffs stretched out along the river.
We took a boat and passed between the rocky cliffs.

examples.ko: 기암절벽의 꼭대기에 작은 정자가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A small pavilion stands at the top of the rocky cliff.
This place is famous for its rocky cliffs and clear water.
Looking at the rocky cliffs made my heart feel refreshed.
In autumn, the maple leaves turn beautifully colored on the rocky cliffs.

explain: '기암괴석'은 모양이 특이한 바위를, '기암절벽'은 그런 바위로 이루어진 벼랑을 말할 때 어울려요. 둘 다 풍경을 설명하는 글에서 잘 만나요.

phrases.en: Strange rocky cliffs continue along the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 절벽이 길게 계속되는 풍경을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes cliffs that continue for a long stretch.

phrases.en: There is a small pavilion on top of the rocky cliff.
phrases.nuance_ko: 절벽 위의 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name a place on top of the cliff.
phrases.en_equiv: on top of a rocky cliff

phrases.en: There are many oddly shaped cliffs on the coast.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기암절벽'을 친구와 말할 때 쉽게 바꿔 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler way to say 기암절벽 when talking with friends.

explain_en: '기암괴석' fits oddly shaped rocks, while '기암절벽' fits a cliff made of such rocks. Both are common in descriptions of scenery.

examples.en: Water drips from the edge of the eaves.

examples.ko: 비가 그치고도 낙숫물 소리가 계속 들렸어요.
examples.en: Even after the rain stopped, I kept hearing the sound of dripping eaves.
I sat on the porch and watched the water dripping from the eaves.
My shoes got completely wet from the dripping eaves.

examples.ko: 낙숫물 떨어지는 자리에 작은 구멍이 생겼어요.
examples.en: A small hole formed where the eave water kept dripping.

examples.ko: 할아버지 집은 낙숫물 소리가 정말 좋았어요.
examples.en: The sound of rain dripping from the eaves at my grandfather's house was really nice.

explain: 주로 한옥처럼 처마가 있는 집에서 비가 처마 끝으로 떨어지는 물을 말해요. 속담에 자주 나오는 말이라 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.example: 매일 조금씩 연습하면 돼요. 낙숫물이 댓돌을 뚫는다잖아요.
phrases.en: Just practice a little every day. They say dripping water wears through the stone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 힘이라도 꾸준히 하면 결국 큰일을 이룬다는 속담이에요. 포기하지 말라고 격려할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that even a small effort, kept up steadily, eventually achieves great things. It is used to encourage someone not to give up.
phrases.en_equiv: Constant dripping wears away the stone.

explain_en: It means water falling from the edge of the eaves, typically on a house with eaves such as a hanok. It appears in a well-known proverb, so it is good to learn them together.

examples.ko: 창문을 열자 하얀 커튼이 천천히 너울거려요.
examples.en: When I open the window, the white curtain sways slowly.

examples.ko: 불꽃이 어둠 속에서 너울거리는 모습이 예뻐요.
examples.en: The flames waving in the dark look pretty.
A flag was waving over the sea.

examples.ko: 긴 치마가 걸을 때마다 너울거려서 시원해 보여요.
examples.en: The long skirt flutters with every step, so it looks cool.

examples.ko: 해초가 물속에서 너울거릴 때마다 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I took a photo every time the seaweed swayed in the water.
The dancer's sleeves flow as the dance goes on.

explain: '펄럭이다'가 바람에 세게 흔들리는 느낌이라면 '너울거리다'는 천, 불꽃, 해초가 부드럽고 느리게 크게 흔들리는 모습이에요. 주로 글이나 묘사에서 많이 쓰고, 말할 때는 '살랑거리다'나 '흔들리다'를 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: Watching the flickering flames makes me feel calm.
phrases.nuance_ko: '너울거리다'를 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸미는 말로 바꾼 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb turned into a modifier that describes the noun after it.

phrases.en: When the wind blows, the curtain waves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 지금 보이는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for describing something you see right now.

phrases.en: The seaweed waved slowly in the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 본 장면을 말할 때 쓰는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form for a scene you already saw.

explain_en: While '펄럭이다' feels like something flapping hard in the wind, '너울거리다' describes cloth, flames or seaweed swaying softly, slowly and widely. It is mostly used in writing and description; in speech people also say '살랑거리다' or '흔들리다'.

examples.ko: 산길을 걷다가 노루를 한 마리 만났어요.
examples.en: I ran into a roe deer while walking on the mountain trail.
The roe deer saw a person and ran away fast.
A roe deer is smaller than a deer.
The children fed grass to the roe deer at the zoo.
I found roe deer tracks in the forest.

examples.ko: 노루 한 마리가 길을 건너서 차가 멈췄어요.
examples.en: A roe deer crossed the road and the cars stopped.

explain: 노루는 산과 숲에 사는 동물로, 사슴보다 몸이 작고 뿔이 짧아요. 도로에 갑자기 나타나는 동물 뉴스에는 '고라니'가 더 자주 나와요. '노루, 사슴, 고라니'는 비슷해 보여서 헷갈려 하는 사람이 많아요.

phrases.en: to be very short; to be tiny
phrases.nuance_ko: 노루 꼬리가 짧은 데서 나온 말로, 시간이 아주 짧을 때 써요. 주로 겨울 해나 낮 이야기에 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: From the roe deer's short tail; used when time is very short, mostly about short winter days.

explain_en: A 노루 is a forest and mountain animal, smaller than a 사슴 (deer) with short antlers. In news about animals suddenly appearing on roads, 고라니 (water deer) comes up more often. Many people mix up 노루, 사슴 and 고라니.

examples.ko: 하늘에서 뇌성이 울리자 아이가 울음을 터뜨렸어요.
examples.en: When thunder rolled across the sky, the child burst into tears.

examples.ko: 뇌성 소리에 강아지가 침대 밑으로 숨었어요.
examples.en: At the sound of thunder, the puppy hid under the bed.
A shower poured down together with a clap of thunder.

examples.ko: 성우는 뇌성이 울린 쪽 하늘을 쳐다보았어요.
examples.en: Seongu looked at the part of the sky where the thunder had sounded.

examples.ko: 뇌성은 번개가 친 뒤에 늦게 들려요.
examples.en: Thunder is heard a little later, after the lightning strikes.

examples.ko: 뇌성처럼 큰 박수 소리가 터져 나왔어요.
examples.en: Applause as loud as thunder burst out.

explain: '천둥소리'와 같은 현상을 가리키지만 뇌성은 한자어라 글이나 딱딱한 말에서 보여요. 일상에서는 '천둥이 치다'라고 훨씬 자연스럽게 말해요.

phrases.en: A peal of thunder suddenly rang out and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천둥 소리가 크게 들릴 때 쓰는 글 같은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A somewhat literary phrase for when thunder rings out loudly.

phrases.en: Thunder and lightning struck, and then rain poured down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천둥과 벼락이 함께 크게 치는 모습을 말하는 글 같은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A literary word for thunder and lightning striking together fiercely.

phrases.example: 밤새 천둥소리 때문에 잠을 못 잤어요.
phrases.en: I couldn't sleep all night because of the thunder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뇌성과 같은 뜻이지만 일상에서는 이 말을 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 뇌성, but much more common in daily speech.

explain_en: It refers to the same thing as '천둥소리' (the sound of thunder), but 뇌성 is a Sino-Korean word seen more in writing and formal speech. In daily life people say '천둥이 치다' much more naturally.

examples.en: The sun is slowly sinking below the horizon.
I walked while watching the sunset slowly fade.

examples.ko: 산 너머로 해가 뉘엿뉘엿 저물어 가요.
examples.en: The sun is slowly setting behind the mountain.

examples.ko: 저녁이 되어 해가 뉘엿뉘엿 기울기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Evening came and the sun began to sink slowly.

examples.ko: 뉘엿뉘엿 해 지는 바다가 정말 예뻤어요.
examples.en: The sea with the sun slowly setting was really beautiful.

examples.ko: 퇴근길에 뉘엿뉘엿 지는 해를 한참 바라봤어요.
examples.en: On my way home from work, I watched the setting sun for a long time.

explain: 해가 지는 모습에만 쓰는 말이에요. '해가 뉘엿뉘엿 지다/넘어가다/기울다'처럼 말하고, 천천히 저무는 느낌이 있어서 달이나 사람의 움직임에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: The sun is slowly setting, so let's go home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 부사와 가장 자주 쓰는 기본 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic and frequent pairing with this adverb.

phrases.en: The sun is slowly going down behind the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해가 산이나 지평선 너머로 천천히 내려가는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The sun sinking slowly beyond a mountain or horizon.
phrases.en_equiv: to slowly sink out of sight

phrases.example: 해가 뉘엿뉘엿 기울 때 산책을 시작했어요.
phrases.en: I started my walk as the sun was slowly sinking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해가 서쪽으로 기우는 때를 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Marks the time when the sun leans toward the west.

explain_en: This word is only for the sun setting. You say '해가 뉘엿뉘엿 지다/넘어가다/기울다', and it has a slow, gradual feel, so it is not used for the moon or for people's movements.

en: to dangle; to swing; to sway

examples.en: The doll attached to my bag dangles and swings.
An icicle is dangling from the edge of the eaves.

examples.ko: 아이가 의자에 앉아서 다리를 대롱거리며 놀아요.
examples.en: The child sits on the chair swinging his legs.
Persimmons dangling from the branches look pretty.
The keychain dangles outside my pocket, which is annoying.
The wind chime hanging on the string swayed in the wind.

explain: 작고 가벼운 물건이 매달려 흔들리는 모습에 써요. '대롱대롱'이라고 반복해서 말하는 일이 많고, 사람의 다리나 열쇠고리, 열매 같은 것에 잘 어울려요. 매달려 있다는 것이 핵심이라서 그냥 흔들리기만 하는 것에는 '흔들리다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Persimmons hang dangling from the tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대롱거리다'의 모양을 흉내 낸 부사로, 매달려 흔들리는 모습을 그려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The mimetic adverb for 대롱거리다, picturing something hanging and swaying.

phrases.en: The keyring dangling from the bag is cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 '-는' 형태로 바꿔 명사를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb in the -는 form modifying a noun.

phrases.en: Fruit is hanging on the branch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그냥 달려 있다는 뜻이라서 '대롱거리다'처럼 흔들린다는 느낌은 없어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Just means hanging, without the swaying feel of 대롱거리다.

explain_en: It describes something small and light hanging and swinging. People often repeat it as '대롱대롱', and it suits things like legs, keychains, and fruit. The key is that it hangs; for something that just shakes, use '흔들리다'.

examples.ko: 산길에 돌무더기가 쌓여 있어서 조심해서 걸었어요.
examples.en: There was a pile of stones on the mountain path, so I walked carefully.
After the earthquake, the house turned into a heap of rubble.
It's dangerous to climb on a pile of stones.

examples.ko: 길가 돌무더기에 작은 소원 돌을 얹었어요.
examples.en: I placed a small wish stone on the roadside stone pile.

examples.ko: 공사장 한쪽에 돌무더기가 아직 치워지지 않았어요.
examples.en: A heap of stones at one side of the construction site hasn't been cleared yet.
We moved the pile of stones one by one and made a path.

explain: '무더기'는 한곳에 수북이 쌓인 더미를 말해서, 돌이 한데 쌓인 모습을 그대로 나타내요. 같은 방식으로 '흙무더기', '쓰레기 무더기'처럼도 말해요. 돌을 일부러 쌓은 탑이 아니라 그냥 쌓여 있는 더미라는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 비가 많이 와서 길 위에 돌무더기가 쌓였어요.
phrases.en: After the heavy rain, a pile of stones built up on the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌이 저절로 모여 쌓인 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes stones that have piled up on their own.

phrases.en: The residents cleared away the pile of stones together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌓인 돌을 없애는 일을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used for removing a pile of stones.

phrases.en: A small flower bloomed among the stone pile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌이 쌓인 곳의 틈이나 안쪽을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to the gaps or inside of a stone pile.

explain_en: '무더기' means a heap piled up in one place, so this describes stones lying together. The same pattern works for '흙무더기' (heap of soil) or '쓰레기 무더기' (pile of trash). It feels like a loose heap rather than a stone tower built on purpose.

examples.en: The cherry blossoms are in full bloom, so the whole neighborhood is pink.
In late April, azaleas and apricot blossoms are in full bloom.

examples.ko: 올해 벚꽃은 이달 말에 만개할 것으로 보여요.
examples.en: This year's cherry blossoms are expected to be in full bloom at the end of this month.

examples.ko: 꽃이 만개하기 전에 한 번 더 가 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'd like to go once more before the flowers are in full bloom.
I heard that the plum blossoms are already in full bloom.

examples.ko: 활짝 만개한 장미가 정원을 가득 채웠어요.
examples.en: Roses in full bloom filled the garden.

explain: 일상에서는 '활짝 피다'라고 말하고, 만개하다는 뉴스나 글에서 많이 써요. 비유로 문화나 재능이 한창 꽃필 때도 '만개하다'라고 해요. 꽃이 피기 시작하는 '개화하다'와 구분해요.

phrases.en: I walked slowly along the path of fully bloomed flowers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '만개하다'를 꾸미는 말로 바꿔 명사 앞에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb as a modifier placed before a noun.

phrases.en: With spring, the flowers bloomed wide open.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 쉽게 말할 때 쓰는 같은 뜻의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday phrase with the same meaning.

phrases.example: 꽃이 만개하기 전에 사진을 찍으러 가요.
phrases.en: Let's go take photos before the flowers fully bloom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 때를 말하는 연결형으로 계획을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A linking form for timing, used when making plans.

explain_en: In daily life people say '활짝 피다', while 만개하다 is common in news and writing. It is also used figuratively when culture or talent flourishes. Keep it separate from '개화하다', which means starting to bloom.

en: to be clear; to be crystal; to be limpid

examples.en: The baby's eyes are so clear, like marbles.

examples.ko: 비가 그치고 나니 하늘이 말갛게 개었어요.
examples.en: After the rain stopped, the sky cleared up bright and clean.

examples.ko: 말간 국물이 먹고 싶어서 맑은 탕을 시켰어요.
examples.en: I wanted a clear broth, so I ordered the clear soup.
My little brother's face looks fresh and clear after washing up.

examples.ko: 시냇물이 바닥이 보일 만큼 말개서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised that the stream was so clear you could see the bottom.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 눈이 말갛고 피부가 하얘요.
examples.en: That child has clear eyes and fair skin.

explain: '맑다'는 날씨, 물, 소리 등에 두루 쓰지만, '말갛다'는 물이나 국물, 눈, 얼굴이 흐리지 않고 투명하게 깨끗한 느낌을 말할 때 써요. ㅎ 불규칙이라 모음 앞에서는 ㅎ이 빠져 '말개요, 말간'이 되고, '말갛고, 말갛게'는 그대로예요.

phrases.en: The clear broth is refreshing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때는 '말간'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 말간 when modifying a noun.

phrases.en: The baby's eyes are clear and pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고'로 이으면 다른 모습과 함께 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linking with -고 lets you add another quality.

phrases.en: This water isn't very clear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깨끗하지 않고 흐릴 때 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form for when something is cloudy rather than clear.

explain_en: '맑다' is used broadly for weather, water and sounds, while '말갛다' describes liquid, broth, eyes or a face that looks clean and see-through. It is a ㅎ-irregular word: the ㅎ drops before a vowel ('말개요', '말간'), while '말갛고' and '말갛게' stay the same.

examples.en: When I shouted on top of the mountain, an echo came back.

examples.ko: 동굴에서는 작은 소리도 메아리로 길게 들려요.
examples.en: In a cave, even small sounds are heard as a long echo.

examples.ko: 아이는 메아리를 듣고 신나서 또 소리쳤어요.
examples.en: The child heard the echo, got excited, and shouted again.
My shout faded away like an echo.
Echoes are heard best in the mountains.
The sound of the echo got smaller and smaller.

explain: '야호!' 하고 산에서 외치면 돌아오는 소리예요. 한국에서는 '메아리가 울리다', '메아리치다'처럼 써요. 말이나 생각이 오래 마음에 남을 때 '마음속에 메아리친다'고 비유해요.

phrases.en: My voice echoed through the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 동사로 바꾼 말로, 소리가 되돌아올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, used when a sound comes back.

phrases.en: The echo rang loudly inside the cave.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 퍼지며 울리는 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Conveys the feeling of a sound spreading and resonating.

phrases.en: When I shouted 'Yaho!', the echo came back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외친 소리가 다시 들릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the sound you shouted is heard again.

explain_en: It is the sound that comes back when you shout '야호!' in the mountains. Koreans say '메아리가 울리다' or '메아리치다'. When words or thoughts stay in your heart for a long time, people say figuratively that they '마음속에 메아리친다'.

examples.en: A pastoral countryside landscape spread out outside the window.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 사진으로 보면 정말 목가적이에요.
examples.en: This village looks really idyllic in photos.
I read a book in a cafe with a pastoral atmosphere.
That movie portrayed the countryside in an idyllic way.

examples.ko: 실제 농촌 생활은 그렇게 목가적이지 않아요.
examples.en: Real rural life isn't that idyllic.

examples.ko: 봄에 가면 더 목가적일 것 같아요.
examples.en: It would probably look even more idyllic if you go in spring.

explain: 평화롭고 한가한 시골의 느낌을 말할 때 쓰고, 조금 이상화된 느낌도 있어요. '목가적인 풍경', '목가적이다'처럼 '-적'이 붙은 말로 써요.

phrases.en: That café has a pastoral atmosphere, so it feels relaxing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시골처럼 평화롭고 한가한 느낌의 장소나 분위기에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for places or atmospheres that feel peaceful and rural.

phrases.en: I want to live a pastoral life after I retire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용한 시골에서 사는 삶을 이상적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe an idealized quiet country life.

phrases.example: 그 화가는 시골 마을을 목가적으로 그렸어요.
phrases.en: That painter depicted the village in a pastoral way.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-으로'를 붙여 어떤 것을 평화로운 시골 느낌으로 표현한다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -으로, it means depicting something in a peaceful, rural way.

explain_en: It describes the peaceful, relaxed feel of the countryside, often with a slightly idealized sense. It is used in the '-적' pattern, as in '목가적인 풍경' or '목가적이다'.

examples.en: When the boat passed, spray rose high.
The waves hit the rocks and threw up spray.
My clothes got soaked in the waterfall's spray.
A rainbow was visible through the spray.
The boat disappeared, leaving only white spray behind.
Spray sparkles when it catches the sunlight.

explain: 파도, 폭포, 배, 수영할 때 물이 부서져 흩어지며 튀어 오르는 작은 물방울들이에요. '물방울'은 하나하나의 방울이고, '물보라'는 여러 방울이 흩날리는 모습 전체를 말해요. '물보라를 일으키다', '물보라가 튀다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 폭포 앞에 서니 물보라가 얼굴에 튀었어요.
phrases.en: Standing in front of the waterfall, spray splashed on my face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물방울이 사방으로 튈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when droplets splash in all directions.

phrases.example: 배 뒤로 하얀 물보라가 길게 이어졌어요.
phrases.en: A long trail of white spray followed behind the boat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색깔 말과 함께 모습을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with a color word to paint the scene.

phrases.en: I stood by the waves and got hit by the spray.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 물방울을 맞을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person is hit by the droplets.

explain_en: It is the many small droplets that break up and fly into the air from waves, waterfalls, boats or swimming. '물방울' is a single drop, while '물보라' is the whole scene of droplets scattering. Common patterns are '물보라를 일으키다' (throw up spray) and '물보라가 튀다' (spray splashes).

examples.en: They say the First Emperor sent people to find the herb of eternal youth.

examples.ko: 옛이야기에서 주인공은 불로초를 찾아 산으로 갔어요.
examples.en: In the old tale, the hero went to the mountains to find the herb of eternal youth.

examples.ko: 이 인삼이 불로초 같다고 할머니가 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother said this ginseng is like an elixir herb.

examples.ko: 불로초는 실제로 있는 풀이 아니라 상상 속의 풀이에요.
examples.en: The herb of eternal youth is not a real plant but an imagined one.

examples.ko: 불로초를 먹으면 늙지 않는다는 이야기가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a story that you stop aging if you eat the herb of eternal youth.
In the comic, a fight broke out over the herb of eternal youth.

explain: 원래는 전설 속의 풀이지만 영지버섯 같은 귀한 약재를 '불로초'라고 부르기도 해요. 몸에 아주 좋은 것을 비유로 '불로초 같다'고도 말해요.

phrases.example: 왕은 불로초를 구하려고 신하를 먼 섬으로 보냈어요.
phrases.en: The king sent his servants to a far island to get the herb of eternal youth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전설 속 풀을 얻으려 한다는 뜻으로 옛이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means trying to obtain the legendary herb; common in old tales.
phrases.en_equiv: to seek the herb of eternal youth

phrases.en: They say a woodcutter dug up the herb of eternal youth deep in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풀이나 약초를 땅에서 캔다는 짝말이라 '불로초'와 자연스럽게 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural pairing with digging up herbs from the ground.
phrases.en_equiv: to dig up the herb of eternal youth

phrases.example: 이 차는 몸에 아주 좋아서 불로초 같아요.
phrases.en: This tea is so good for the body that it's like a magic herb.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 아주 좋은 것을 비유로 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative compliment for something very good for the body.
phrases.en_equiv: to be like a magic herb

explain_en: It is originally a legendary plant, but valued medicinal items such as ganoderma (영지버섯) are also called '불로초'. People also say '불로초 같다' figuratively about something very good for the body.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 몇 번이나 되살아나서 불사조라고 불려요.
examples.en: That team came back to life so many times that it is called a phoenix.

examples.ko: 불사조는 재 속에서 다시 태어난다는 전설의 새예요.
examples.en: The phoenix is a legendary bird said to be reborn from ashes.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 불사조처럼 다시 무대에 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: That singer came back to the stage like a phoenix.

examples.ko: 영화 속 불사조가 하늘로 날아오르는 장면이 멋졌어요.
examples.en: The scene of the phoenix soaring into the sky in the movie was cool.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 야구부는 불사조 같은 팀이에요.
examples.en: Our school's baseball club is a team that never dies.

examples.ko: 불사조 이야기를 처음 들은 건 어릴 때였어요.
examples.en: I first heard the story of the phoenix when I was little.

explain: 영어의 phoenix와 같은 새이고 '피닉스'라고도 해요. 어려움을 이기고 계속 살아나는 사람이나 팀을 칭찬하며 비유할 때 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.example: 그 가수는 불사조 같아요. 몇 번 쓰러져도 다시 일어나요.
phrases.en: That singer is like a phoenix. Even after falling several times, they get back up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려움을 이기고 다시 살아나는 사람을 칭찬하는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative compliment for someone who overcomes hardship and revives.

phrases.en: That company came back to life like a phoenix.
phrases.nuance_ko: '처럼'을 붙여 되살아나는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '처럼', describes the way something rises back to life.

phrases.en: The phoenix is a bird that is reborn from fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영어에서 온 이름이고 같은 새를 가리켜요. 이야기나 게임에서 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The English-derived name for the same bird; often heard in stories and games.

explain_en: It is the same bird as the English 'phoenix', also called '피닉스' in Korean. It is also used as a compliment for a person or team that keeps coming back after hardship.

examples.en: The chicks are peeping in the yard.
The chick was cheeping from morning, so I woke up early.
The baby bird waits for its mother, cheeping.
The sound of chicks peeping is so cute.
The chicks in the box peeped all night.
The kids follow me chirping like chicks.

explain: 병아리나 아주 어린 새가 가늘고 짧게 우는 소리예요. 아이들이 귀엽게 재잘거릴 때 비유로 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: The chicks cheep 'ppiak ppiak'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병아리 소리를 흉내 낸 말로, 소리가 반복될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sound word imitating chicks, used when the sound repeats.

phrases.en: I can hear a cheeping sound inside the box.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삐악거리다'의 활용형으로, 소리를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form describing the sound.

phrases.en: The chicks chirp every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새나 병아리가 소리를 낼 때도 '울다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Ulda' is also used for chicks and birds making sounds.

explain_en: It is the thin, short cry of chicks or very young birds. It is sometimes used figuratively when children chatter in a cute way.

examples.en: Our village lies at the foot of the mountain.
A small cafe opened on the mountain's lower slope.
The fog came down all the way to the foot of the mountain.
A stream flows where the foot of the mountain ends.

examples.ko: 산자락을 따라 걷다 보면 작은 절이 나와요.
examples.en: If you walk along the foothills, you'll come to a small temple.
These apples were grown on the mountain slope, so they taste great.

explain: 산이 평지와 만나는 아랫부분을 말하며 '산기슭'과 거의 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. '산자락 아래 마을'처럼 마을이나 집의 위치를 말할 때 자주 써요. 부드럽고 정겨운 느낌이라 글이나 여행 소개에서도 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: There is a small temple at the foot of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산자락'과 거의 같은 뜻이지만 조금 더 일반적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as '산자락', but a bit more general.

phrases.en: If you walk along the foot of the mountain, the view is nice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길이나 마을이 산 아랫부분을 따라 이어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a road or village follows the lower part of a mountain.

phrases.en: The village at the foot of the mountain has clean air.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산 아래에 있는 조용한 마을을 소개할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to introduce a quiet village below a mountain.

explain_en: It means the lower part of a mountain where it meets flat land, and can almost be swapped with '산기슭'. It is often used for locating villages or houses, as in '산자락 아래 마을'. It has a soft, warm feel, so it also appears a lot in writing and travel descriptions.

examples.ko: 비가 그치자 가까운 곳에서 소쩍새가 울었어요.
examples.en: When the rain stopped, a scops owl called nearby.
Every night I hear a scops owl from the mountain.
Scops owls rest in the day and are active at night.

examples.ko: 시골 할머니 댁에서 소쩍새 울음을 처음 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard a scops owl's call for the first time at my grandmother's countryside house.
I've never seen a scops owl in person.
I recorded the sound of a scops owl calling.

explain: 올빼미 종류의 작은 새로, 밤에 울어서 소리로 먼저 알게 되는 경우가 많아요. 울음소리를 '소쩍소쩍'으로 흉내 내요. 시나 노래, 소설의 시골 밤 장면에 나오기도 해요.

phrases.en: I heard a 'sojjeok-sojjeok' sound all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소쩍새 울음소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An imitation of the scops owl's call.

phrases.en: The scops owl's cry spread across the quiet mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새가 우는 소리를 명사로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name the bird's cry as a noun.

phrases.en: Owls are birds that are active at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소쩍새가 속한 더 넓은 종류의 새를 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name for the broader type of bird that includes the scops owl.

explain_en: It is a small owl-type bird, and since it calls at night you often notice it by sound first. Its call is imitated as '소쩍소쩍'. It sometimes appears in poems, songs and country night scenes in novels.

examples.ko: 가을이 되면 산에 억새가 하얗게 피어요.
examples.en: In autumn, silver grass blooms white on the mountains.
The silver grass swaying in the wind is beautiful.
Shall we go to the mountain this weekend to see the silver grass?

examples.ko: 억새 사이로 난 길을 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: I slowly walked along the path through the silver grass.
The silvery grass glittered in the sunset.
On Jeju Island there are many hills famous for silver grass.

explain: 가을 산과 들의 풍경을 말할 때 자주 나오는 식물이에요. 물가에서 자라는 '갈대'와 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 억새는 주로 산이나 들에서 볼 수 있어요. 보통 '억새가 피다', '억새가 흔들리다'처럼 가을 분위기와 함께 말해요.

phrases.en: The silver grass flowers blow white in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 억새에 피는 꽃 부분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the flowering plumes of the grass.

phrases.en: The silver grass sways when the wind blows.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가을 풍경을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when describing an autumn scene.

phrases.en: I'm going to see the silver grass this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가을 나들이 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about an autumn outing.

explain_en: This plant often appears when people describe autumn scenery on mountains and fields. It is easy to confuse with '갈대' (reed), which grows near water, while '억새' is mainly seen on mountains and fields. It is usually used with an autumn mood, as in '억새가 피다' and '억새가 흔들리다'.

examples.en: I scooped up water and drank it at a small spring in the mountains.
The water from the small spring is very clear and cool.
I found a small spring while hiking.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 할머니 댁 뒷산에 옹달샘이 있었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, there was a small spring on the hill behind my grandmother's house.
Let's rest for a moment in front of the spring before we go.
I was curious about the spring in the children's song, so I looked it up.

explain: '우물'은 사람이 땅을 파서 만들지만, 옹달샘은 산이나 숲에서 물이 저절로 솟아요. 그냥 '샘'보다 작고 오목해서 아담한 느낌이 들어요. 동요 가사 '깊은 산속 옹달샘' 덕분에 한국 사람들에게 친숙해요.

phrases.example: 옹달샘 물을 한 모금 마셨더니 정말 시원했어요.
phrases.en: I took a sip of the spring water and it was really refreshing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어 뒤에 '물'을 붙여 샘에서 나오는 물을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 물 to the headword refers to the water that comes from the spring.

phrases.en: A rabbit is drinking water at the small spring deep in the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동요 가사처럼 산이나 숲에 있는 작은 샘을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing, as in the children's song, for a small spring in the mountains or woods.

phrases.en: You can drink this spring water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기와 상관없이 샘에서 나오는 물을 가리키는 더 넓은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word for water from any spring, regardless of size.

explain_en: A '우물' (well) is dug by people, but an 옹달샘 wells up by itself in the mountains or woods. It is smaller and shallower than a plain '샘', so it feels cozy. Koreans know it well from the children's song lyric '깊은 산속 옹달샘'.

en: to chirp; to sing; to twitter

examples.en: Every morning birds sing in the trees.
I woke up to the sound of birds chirping.

examples.ko: 숲 속에서 새들이 즐겁게 우짖고 있어요.
examples.en: Birds are chirping happily in the forest.
The bird that had been chirping since dawn has gone quiet.

examples.ko: 참새 한 마리가 베란다에서 우짖다가 날아갔어요.
examples.en: A sparrow chirped on the balcony and then flew away.

examples.ko: 새들이 우짖으면 봄이 온 것 같아요.
examples.en: When birds chirp, it feels like spring has come.

explain: 새가 소리 내는 것에 쓰는 글말 느낌의 표현이라 시나 글에서 자주 나와요. 일상 말로는 '새가 울다'라고 하고, 작은 새가 가볍게 소리 내는 것은 '지저귀다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I greeted the morning to the sound of birds chirping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여 새소리를 글말처럼 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun to describe birdsong in a literary way.

phrases.en: Birds are chirping in the forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새가 지금 소리 내고 있는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for birds chirping right now.

phrases.en: A little bird twitters outside the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우짖다'와 비슷하지만 작은 새가 가볍게 우는 느낌이 더 커요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 우짖다 but suggests a small bird's light singing.

explain_en: It is a somewhat literary word for birds making sounds, common in poems and writing. In daily speech people say '새가 울다', and '지저귀다' is used for small birds chirping lightly.

en: to be colorful; to be picturesque

examples.ko: 우리는 벽을 짙은 색깔로 울긋불긋하게 꾸몄어요.
examples.en: We decorated the wall in deep colors, making it colorful.
The living room is so colorful that my eyes feel dizzy.
The mountain is a blaze of color with the autumn leaves.

examples.ko: 울긋불긋한 옷을 입으니 눈에 확 띄어요.
examples.en: Wearing such colorful clothes really makes you stand out.
The colorful leaves have all fallen.

examples.ko: 산이 가장 울긋불긋할 때 사진을 찍어요.
examples.en: Let's take photos when the mountain is at its most colorful.

explain: 색이 여러 가지로 섞여 화려할 때 써요. '울긋불긋한 옷', '울긋불긋하게 꾸미다'처럼 뒤에 오는 말에 맞춰 활용해요. 너무 요란해서 정신없다는 느낌으로 말할 때도 있어요.

phrases.en: The autumn mountain is a blaze of color.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장 끝에서 현재 모습을 말하는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite present-tense form used to end a sentence.

phrases.en: People in brightly colored clothes walked by.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.example: 이 옷은 울긋불긋하지 않아서 입기 편해요.
phrases.en: These clothes aren't flashy, so they're comfortable to wear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이 차분하고 화려하지 않을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form used when colors are calm and not flashy.

explain_en: It is used when many colors mix into a gaudy, bright look. Conjugate it to fit what follows, as in '울긋불긋한 옷' or '울긋불긋하게 꾸미다'. It can also carry a sense of being so flashy it feels busy.

examples.en: Ducks float leisurely across the lake.
He walked calmly through the crowd.
Clouds drift lazily across the sky.
Even though he's late for the exam, he's eating calmly.

examples.ko: 강물이 유유히 흐르는 모습을 한참 바라봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the river flow slowly for a long time.
The cat strolled unhurriedly along the top of the wall.

explain: '천천히'는 속도만 말하지만, '유유히'는 서두르지 않고 여유 있는 모습까지 담아요. 급한 상황인데도 태연한 사람에게 쓰면 '느긋하다, 뻔뻔하다'는 느낌도 나요. 사람, 동물, 강물, 구름처럼 천천히 움직이는 것에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The river flows along leisurely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강이나 구름처럼 느긋하게 움직이는 것에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits well with things like rivers and clouds that move calmly.

phrases.en: The thief disappeared without any hurry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 급한 상황인데도 태연한 모습에 쓰면 뻔뻔한 느낌도 나요.
phrases.nuance_en: In a tense situation it also gives a sense of nerve and nonchalance.

phrases.en: I drank coffee leisurely on the weekend morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '유유히' 대신 많이 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word often used instead of 'yuyuhi' in daily talk.

explain_en: '천천히' only describes speed, but '유유히' also carries the sense of being unhurried and at ease. Used for someone calm in an urgent situation, it can also suggest coolness or even nerve. It suits slow-moving things such as people, animals, rivers and clouds.

examples.ko: 가을이 되면 벼 이삭이 노랗게 익어요.
examples.en: In autumn the rice ears ripen to yellow.

examples.ko: 농부가 밀 이삭을 한 줌 잘라 왔어요.
examples.en: The farmer cut a handful of wheat ears and brought them.
The ears of grain bow their heads as they ripen.
I carefully picked up even the ears that had fallen in the field.
The wind blows between the barley ears.
I shook the grains of rice off the ear.

explain: 이삭은 벼, 보리, 밀처럼 곡식 줄기 끝에만 써요. 과일이나 채소에 달린 건 '열매'라고 해요. '벼 이삭', '보리 이삭'처럼 곡식 이름을 앞에 붙여요. 성경 속 인물 이름(Isaac)도 같은 글자예요.

phrases.en: The barley ears sway in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곡식 이름을 앞에 붙여 어떤 곡식인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The grain name goes in front to say which grain it is.

phrases.en: After the harvest, I picked up leftover grain ears in the field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거두고 남은 곡식을 주울 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This phrase is for picking up grain left after the harvest.

phrases.en: When the grain ears ripen, we begin the harvest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곡식이 속까지 잘 차고 익었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is used when the grain is fully formed and ripe.

explain_en: 이삭 is used only for the top of a grain stalk such as rice, barley, or wheat. What hangs on fruit or vegetable plants is called 열매. The grain name goes in front, as in 벼 이삭 and 보리 이삭. The Bible name Isaac is written with the same letters.

en: to waver; to sway; to shake

examples.en: Moonlight shimmers and sways on the lake.

examples.ko: 촛불이 바람에 일렁거리며 벽에 그림자를 만들었어요.
examples.en: The candle flame wavered in the wind and cast shadows on the wall.
I watched the ripples sway for a long time.
The lights flickered, and my eyes hurt.
I felt an excitement that made my heart stir.

examples.ko: 수영장 바닥 무늬가 물에 일렁거려 보여요.
examples.en: The pattern on the pool floor looks wavy through the water.

explain: 물결, 불빛, 그림자처럼 부드럽게 흔들리는 것에 써요. '흔들리다'보다 잔잔하고 일정하게 출렁이는 느낌이고, '일렁이다'와 거의 같게 써요.

phrases.en: Moonlight is wavering on the lake.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일렁거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 더 짧아서 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 일렁거리다, but shorter and more common in speech.

phrases.en: I can see a wavering light through the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 '-는' 형태로 바꿔 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-는' form of the verb, used to describe a noun that follows.

phrases.en: When the wind blows, the ripples on the pond sway.
phrases.nuance_ko: '물결'과 함께 가장 자연스럽게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing, with 물결 (ripples) as the subject.

explain_en: It is used for things that sway softly, like ripples, lights and shadows. It feels gentler and more rhythmic than '흔들리다', and it can be used almost the same as '일렁이다'.

examples.ko: 한복 자락을 살짝 잡고 계단을 올랐어요.
examples.en: I held up the hem of my hanbok slightly and climbed the stairs.
The skirts of my coat flapped wildly in the wind.

examples.ko: 산 자락에 작은 절이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small temple at the foot of the mountain.

examples.ko: 커튼 자락 사이로 아침 햇빛이 들어왔어요.
examples.en: Morning sunlight came in through a gap in the curtain.
I pulled the edge of the blanket up to cover my neck.

examples.ko: 치마 자락이 길어서 걸을 때 밟을 것 같아요.
examples.en: The hem of this skirt is long, so I might step on it when I walk.

explain: 옷, 이불, 커튼처럼 길게 늘어진 아랫부분을 가리켜요. 산의 아래쪽 비탈에도 써서 '산 자락'이라고 해요. '옷자락', '치맛자락', '산자락'처럼 붙여 쓰는 말이 많아요.

phrases.example: 아이가 엄마 옷자락을 꼭 잡고 있어요.
phrases.en: The child is holding tightly onto Mom's hem.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자락'이 앞말과 붙은 형태로, 옷의 늘어진 끝부분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The attached form for the hanging edge of clothing.

phrases.en: The skirt hem dragged on the floor, so I walked carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치마의 아랫부분을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the lower part of a skirt.

phrases.en: There is a small village at the foot of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산의 아래쪽 비탈을 말해요. '산 아래'보다 풍경을 그리는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the lower slope of a mountain; sounds more scenic than 산 아래.

explain_en: It refers to the lower part of things that hang down, such as clothes, blankets and curtains. It is also used for the lower slope of a mountain, as in '산 자락'. Many words are written as one, such as '옷자락', '치맛자락' and '산자락'.

examples.en: Every morning sparrows chirp outside my window.

examples.ko: 새들이 짹짹 노래하는 소리에 잠을 깼어요.
examples.en: I woke up to the sound of birds chirping.

examples.ko: 아기 새들이 짹짹 하고 어미를 불러요.
examples.en: The baby birds call for their mother with chirps.
I can hear a chirping sound from the tree.
Swallows twitter under the eaves.

examples.ko: 창문을 여니 짹짹 소리가 더 크게 났어요.
examples.en: When I opened the window, the chirping sounded louder.

explain: 참새처럼 작은 새가 우는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. 보통 '짹짹 울다/지저귀다'로 쓰고, 소리를 가리킬 때는 '짹짹 소리'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: Sparrows are chirping in the tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: '짹짹'에 '-거리다'를 붙여서 새가 계속 우는 모습을 동사로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-거리다' to '짹짹' makes a verb for a bird chirping continuously.

phrases.en: I can hear chirping outside the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새가 우는 소리 자체를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to the sound of birds chirping itself.

phrases.en: Birds chirp every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '울다'보다 새가 즐겁게 노래하는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compared with '울다', it feels like a bird singing cheerfully.

explain_en: It imitates the cry of small birds like sparrows. It usually appears as '짹짹 울다/지저귀다', and for the sound itself people say '짹짹 소리'.

examples.en: When high tide came, the seawater rose.
I took a walk on a night when the moon was waxing.
We evacuated before the water rose to our waists.
Anticipation welled up in me, and I couldn't sleep.
I barely held back the tears welling up in my eyes.
Water is slowly filling up in the bathtub.

explain: 물이나 감정이 아래에서 위로 천천히 가득 찰 때 써요. '차다'는 가득 찬 상태이고 '차오르다'는 차 올라가는 과정이에요. 그래서 '물이 차오르다', '눈물이 차오르다', '달이 차오르다'처럼 변하는 모습에 어울려요.

phrases.en: Watching a sad movie, tears well up in my eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈물이 천천히 고이는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For tears slowly gathering in the eyes.

phrases.example: 비가 많이 와서 강물이 차오르고 있어요.
phrases.en: It rained a lot, so the river water is rising.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 점점 높아지는 과정을 말할 때 '-고 있다'와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs well with '-고 있다' for water gradually rising.

phrases.en: Joy filled my heart at the news that I passed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기쁨이나 감동이 마음속에 가득해지는 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes joy or emotion filling up inside you.

explain_en: It is for water or feelings slowly filling up from below. '차다' is the full state, while '차오르다' is the process of rising to full. So it fits changing scenes like '물이 차오르다', '눈물이 차오르다', and '달이 차오르다'.

examples.en: The air is crisp and refreshing as I climb the mountain.
A cool, refreshing breeze brushed past my face.
The sound of the valley stream was clear and refreshing.

examples.ko: 비 온 뒤라서 하늘이 청량해 보여요.
examples.en: The sky looks fresh and clear because it just rained.
I like this song because the voice is clear and fresh.
In summer, crisp, cool drinks are popular.

explain: 시원하고 맑아서 상쾌한 느낌에 써요. 공기·바람·소리·음료 광고에 잘 나오는 글말 느낌의 단어라, 일상 대화에서는 '시원하다', '상쾌하다'를 더 많이 해요. '청량음료'처럼 합성어로도 써요.

phrases.en: That singer sings with a clear, refreshing voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맑고 시원하게 들리는 소리를 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise a voice that sounds clear and refreshing.

phrases.en: This drink has a crisp, refreshing taste.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탄산음료나 차가운 음료의 시원하고 깔끔한 맛을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the crisp, clean taste of fizzy or cold drinks.

phrases.en: The sound of the valley stream sounds clear and refreshing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형 '청량하게'로 소리가 맑고 시원하게 느껴진다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form says a sound feels clear and cool to the ear.

explain_en: It describes a cool, clear, refreshing feeling. It has a written tone often seen with air, wind, sound, and drink ads, so daily talk prefers 시원하다 or 상쾌하다. It also appears in compounds like 청량음료 (soft drink).

examples.en: Morning dew is clinging to the blades of grass.
I plucked a blade of grass and held it in my mouth.
The blades of grass sway gently in the wind.
The child made a small boat out of a leaf of grass.
The tip of the grass was sharp and cut my hand.

examples.ko: 비가 그치자 풀잎 냄새가 진하게 났어요.
examples.en: After the rain stopped, there was a strong smell of grass.

explain: '풀'은 식물 전체이고 '풀잎'은 그 풀의 잎 한 장이에요. 이슬이나 바람 장면에서 시처럼 자주 나와요. 나무의 잎은 '나뭇잎'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Morning dew is clinging to the blades of grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이슬이나 물방울과 함께 쓰는 시 같은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A poetic phrase used with dew or water drops.
phrases.en_equiv: to form on a blade of grass

phrases.en: The blades of grass sway in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람 부는 풍경을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to describe a windy scene.

phrases.en: I picked a blade of grass and blew on it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잎 한 장을 셀 때 '하나'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '하나' to count a single blade.

explain_en: 풀 is the plant as a whole, while 풀잎 is a single leaf of it. It shows up often in poetic scenes with dew or wind. A tree's leaf is 나뭇잎.

examples.ko: 새벽이 되자 방 안에 한기가 돌았어요.
examples.en: As dawn came, a chill spread through the room.

examples.ko: 갑자기 한기를 느껴서 두꺼운 옷을 꺼냈어요.
examples.en: I suddenly felt a chill, so I took out a thick coat.
Maybe I caught a cold; I've had the chills since this morning.

examples.ko: 지하 주차장에 들어서자 서늘한 한기에 몸이 움츠러들었어요.
examples.en: When I walked into the underground garage, the cold air made me shrink back.

examples.ko: 난로를 켜도 한기는 쉽게 가시지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even with the heater on, the chill didn't go away easily.

examples.ko: 이불 속에 들어가니 한기도 점점 풀렸어요.
examples.en: Once I got under the blanket, the chill gradually went away too.

explain: '추위'는 날씨 전반의 추움을 말하고, '한기'는 몸으로 느끼는 찬 기운이에요. 몸이 으슬으슬할 때 '한기가 들다'라고 하고, 열이 날 때나 무서울 때의 오싹한 느낌에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I got wet in the rain, so I feel chilly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 으슬으슬할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for feeling chilly in the body.

phrases.en: I can feel a chill from the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디선가 찬 기운이 올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when cold air is felt coming from somewhere.

phrases.en: I blocked the chill with a thick curtain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찬 기운이 들어오지 못하게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for keeping cold air out.

explain_en: '추위' refers to cold weather in general, while '한기' is the cold air you feel in your body. You say '한기가 들다' when you get the shivers, and it can also describe the chilly feeling you get with a fever or when you are scared.

examples.en: Trash floated down with the river from upstream.
Gentle music is drifting in from somewhere.
The stream is flowing toward the village.
Clouds are slowly drifting in from far away.

examples.ko: 바람을 타고 꽃향기가 흘러와서 기분이 좋았어요.
examples.en: The scent of flowers drifted in on the wind and I felt good.

examples.ko: 강을 따라 흘러온 모래가 바닷가에 쌓였어요.
examples.en: Sand that flowed down the river piled up on the beach.

explain: 말하는 사람 쪽으로 다가올 때 써요. 멀어지는 쪽은 '흘러가다'예요. 물뿐 아니라 음악, 냄새, 구름처럼 천천히 퍼져서 오는 것에도 써요.

phrases.en: Soft music is drifting over from next door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 천천히 퍼져서 들려올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when sound spreads slowly and reaches you.

phrases.en: Clear water flows down from upstream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 말하는 사람 쪽으로 흘러올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when water flows toward the speaker.

phrases.en: Clouds are slowly drifting in from the west.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구름처럼 천천히 움직이는 것이 가까이 올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for slow-moving things like clouds coming closer.

explain_en: Use it when something moves toward the speaker. Moving away is '흘러가다'. It applies not only to water but also to music, smells and clouds that spread and arrive slowly.
